Advanced Infrastructure  ·  Infrastructure Design Bought separately. They fail together.

Network and storage are bought separately, operated separately and reviewed separately — and then they fail together. This is the engagement for when the question is bigger than one layer.

8–12 WEEKSTARGET ARCHITECTURE · SEQUENCED PATHWE ASSESS · PARTNERS DELIVER
The decisions underneath

Three questions decide the shape.

An estate has a shape, and the shape is usually an accident of the order things were bought in. These are the three questions that decide whether the shape still fits.

01

What has to be true, regardless of vendor

Requirements written as things a supplier can be held to, before any product is in the room. Most estates have never had this document.

02

Where the layers actually depend on each other

Identity underneath storage underneath recovery. The dependency that breaks you is almost never the one on the diagram.

03

What order to change things in

Sequenced by exposure, not by contract renewal date. The cheapest change is rarely the one that removes the most risk.

The boundary

We design it. We do not run it.

Three moves. Two of them are ours, and the one in the middle deliberately is not.

MOVE 01 — OURS

Assess and specify

We walk the estate, write the requirements the infrastructure has to meet, and sequence the path to get there. The requirement is written before any product is considered.

MOVE 02 — NOT OURS

You contract directly

You hold the contract with the provider or carrier. No margin passes through us, and no lock-in passes through us either. This is the move that makes the other two believable.

MOVE 03 — OURS

Re-test on a cycle

We return and check the estate against the same questions — including whether the thing you bought did what it was specified to do.

Because we carry nothing and resell nothing in this pillar, no recommendation we make depends on which platform you choose.

Questions we are asked

Before you ask us.

How is this different from buying both other services?
The two service reviews each answer a layer well and neither owns the seam. Infrastructure Design starts from the requirement and follows it wherever it goes, which means it will spend time in identity and in contracts — neither of which belongs to either layer review.
We already have an architecture document. Is that not this?
Possibly. The test is whether it states what has to be true independently of what you currently own. Most architecture documents describe an estate; far fewer specify a requirement that a supplier could be held to. If yours does, bring it — the engagement gets shorter.
Do you implement the path you write?
No. Implementation is contracted directly between you and a provider. We come back and check whether what was implemented did what it was specified to do, which is a role we could not hold credibly if we had also done the work.
What if the finding is that nothing needs to change?
Then that is the finding, and it costs the same. A review that can only justify itself by recommending a purchase is not a review.

Start with the answer you got twice, differently.

Thirty minutes. If two suppliers have given you contradictory answers about the same requirement, that contradiction is the fastest way into this conversation.
